July 2024 – Present
•	Study the role of Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis (MS) using molecular biology and immunology techniques
•	Deliver presentations at internal journal clubs and lab meetings to communicate experimental findings 
•	Present original research at the Americas Committee for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis (ACTRIMS) Forum 2025 and at our annual patient symposium (poster presentations)
•	Mentor and train a junior RA and summer intern in laboratory protocols and project running

Research Assistant, Padilla-Benavides Laboratory at Wesleyan University, Middletown, CT  
     September 2021 – May 2024
•	Investigated the relationship between the SWI/SNF protein complex, a chromatin remodeler, and metal responsive transcription factors in the regulation of transition metals in mammalian cells utilizing biochemistry and microbiology laboratory techniques
•	Purified recombinant proteins for protein crystallization experiments 
•	Analyzed and compiled laboratory data for poster presentations and publications as well as collaborated with fellow lab members on experiments and in weekly lab meetings
•	Co-first author on a manuscript currently under review at the Journal of Biological Chemistry: “The PBAF chromatin remodeling complex contributes to metal homeostasis through Mtf1 regulation” 
•	Authored and defended senior honors thesis on the role of mSWI/SNF in metal regulation: “Exploring the Metal Regulatory Dynamics of the mSWI/SNF Complex in Collaboration with Mtf1 in Proliferating Myoblasts” http://www.doi.org/10.14418/wes01.1.2852
